rationale: Recurs lines 1, 8, 28 always governed by ⲡⲓⲉⲣⲟ 'the river' or ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲧⲟⲓⲭⲉⲓⲟⲛ 'of the elements.' Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱⲧ in the substantival sense 'fork, branch, conjunction' or ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'channel/tributary.' Functions as the technical Manichaean term for a tributary-stream of the great river of Judgment. Distinct from ⲡⲁⲥⲉ 'half/portion' and ⲡⲏϣⲉ 'share.'

Lycopolitan ⲗⲉⲣⲟ = ⲓⲉⲣⲟ 'river' + ⲛⲁⲟ 'great' + ⲧⲓⲕⲣⲓⲥ (Greek κρίσις 'judgment,' with prosthetic ⲧⲓ-). Manichaean cosmological term for the punitive river whose branches pour fire into the mouths of bound archons. Capitalized as cosmic principle. Recurs lines 1, 8, 27.
Variant article on same compound. Line 27.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲱⲕϩ̄ 'burn,' parallel to ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ in accumulated vocabulary but with -ⲭϩ instead of -ⲭⲍ. Used both as verb (line 4: ϣⲁϩⲣⲁⲭϩⲟⲩ 'they continually burn them') and noun (line 5: ⲡⲉϩⲣⲱⲭϩ̄ 'his burning'). Variant orthography of established root.

Reduplicated qualitative form of ⲕⲙⲟⲙ 'be black, dark.' Lycopolitan intensifier pattern. Used in punitive-correspondence series at line 18 alongside 'bound, fettered, buried.' Standard reduplicated intensive.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓϣ 'time, season.' Vowel-shift ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓ → ⲟⲁⲓ̈. Line 6 'seasons of [...]' as the temporal frame for archonic dryness without rains.
Already attested in accumulated vocabulary (page 154 not yet processed). Compound: ⲙⲟⲩ ('water') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ϩⲱⲟⲩ ('rain'). Plural here with privative ⲉⲙⲡⲧⲉ 'without' = 'without rains.'
Possible Lycopolitan form of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' or its qualitative ⲙⲉϩ. ⲁⲩⲙⲉϩⲧ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'they were filled together/as one' (line 3). Cognate with ⲡⲉϩⲙⲉϩⲧ̄ 'his filling' (line 4).
Coptic ⲡⲱϣ/ⲡⲁϣⲉ 'half, share, portion.' Cf. ⲡⲁⲥⲉ in accumulated vocabulary. Line 28: 'the share of the branch of the elements.'
Lycopolitan ϣⲁⲣⲡ = ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ 'first.' Line 14: 'first marvel' — the foundational marvel preceding the elect one's reflection on the cosmic god.
